summary: Edge socket exhaustion causing cascading 5xx burst for dedicated tenant
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-10 02:35 UTC multiple customers (reported by NovaHealth) observed elevated 5xx responses from the Redwood API. Errors were concentrated through the edge api-gateway and manifested as 502/503s and aborted streaming sessions. Impact: Customer requests were intermittently failing (high error rate) for ~45 minutes; NovaHealth reported failed inference requests and partial streaming disconnects impacting a live feature. Environment: prod-us-east-1 dedicated pool serving NovaHealth on dedicated infra. Observed behavior: api-gateway returned 502/503; edge proxies showed large numbers of sockets in FIN_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT and Apache/Envoy logs reported "too many open files" and connection accept failures. Expected behavior: sustained request success at normal error rates and stable streaming connections.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate a burst of long-polling streaming sessions from a single tenant (50-100 concurrent short-lived TCP sessions per second) to the hosted API in prod-us-east-1
Observe edge-proxy FD usage (netstat/lsof) and api-gateway responses under the burst
Verify behavior with and without SDK keepalive disabled to replicate aggressive connection churn
logs: [2026-03-10T02:36:14Z] envoy edge0 ERROR: accept() failed: Too many open files (errno=24)
[2026-03-10T02:37:02Z] api-gateway: upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. remote_addr=10.20.30.45
[2026-03-10T02:39:11Z] runtime-gpu-3 INFO: streaming session aborted: client closed connection during prefix-send
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reports a sudden surge in 5xxs starting 02:35 UTC; customer traced to a new client webhook that opened many short-lived streams. Assigned to SRE for triage.

SRE (Marco): Initial triage shows edge proxies hitting ulimit for file descriptors. Kernel accept queue backlog filling; many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT. Hypothesis: connection churn + lowered keepalive causing ephemeral port/socket exhaustion.

SRE (Marco): Rolled temporary mitigations at 02:52 UTC: increased fd limits on edge proxies, applied tcp_tw_reuse and tuned net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout to reduce TIME_WAIT accumulation. Observed drop in new 5xxs after 02:58 UTC.
Customer (NovaHealth): Confirmed that failures dropped after 02:58 UTC and application errors returned to baseline. Customer still needs root-cause details and actions to prevent recurrence.
Eng (Elena Ruiz): Noted a recent config change in infra PR #1427 which adjusted the api-gateway keepalive policy (reduced idle keepalive window). Rolling that change back as a precaution.
investigation_notes: Correlation: high request churn from a single tenant SDK version 1.2.8 that disables persistent keepalive; coincided with infra change to reduce keepalive timeout the day prior.
Edge proxy metrics: FD usage peaked at 98% of ulimit during the burst; accept queue length reached configured max backlog and new accepts were dropped.
Runtime metrics: serving-runtime pods experienced increased connect/disconnect events but remained within CPU/GPU capacity; no OOMs observed.

Hypothesis validated: combination of client churn + reduced keepalive window caused socket lifecycle turnover to spike, exhausting kernel resources on edge proxies leading to connection failures and 5xx responses.
Checked related tickets for similar symptoms: SUP-62111 (tenant burst connection queueing) showed similar pattern but was earlier and had different mitigation applied.
Gathered packet captures and netstat snapshots, stored in S3: s3://redwood-ops/investigations/SUP-825410/
Monitoring gaps uncovered: we did not have an automated alert for FD-usage > 85% on edge proxies; created a follow-up to add this alert.
resolution: Short-term mitigations applied (02:52-02:58 UTC): increased file descriptor ulimit on edge proxies, tuned tcp_tw_reuse and tcp_fin_timeout, temporarily increased accept backlog where possible.
Rollback: reverted the keepalive reduction change from infra PR github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1427 to restore previous connection reuse behavior.
Rate-limiting: applied tenant-level soft limits for streaming session churn to protect shared edge resources for dedicated pools while we deploy a permanent fix.
Permanent fix: engineering to harden edge proxy to fail fast with quota-aware responses, add backpressure at api-gateway and add fd-usage autoscaling behavior for proxies in dedicated clusters.
Customer communication: notified NovaHealth of mitigations and planned follow-ups.
root_cause: A recent api-gateway keepalive policy change combined with an increase in short-lived streaming connections from the tenant's SDK caused excessive connection churn, exhausting edge proxy file descriptors and accept queues, producing downstream 5xx errors.
follow_up_tasks: INFRA-2983: Add FD-usage >85% alert for edge proxies (owner: infra)
SERVE-447: Implement tenant-level streaming connection backpressure and quota enforcement (owner: serving-runtime)
OPS-762: Document safe keepalive defaults and add pre-deploy checklist item for connection-related tuning (owner: platform-ops)
COMM-120: Share postmortem with NovaHealth and include recommended SDK/keepalive settings (owner: Customer Success)
SEC-45: Evaluate whether monitoring and alerting should be extended to dedicated tenant-specific edge clusters (owner: reliability)
